According to an update issued by the International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) on November 5, the approximately one-month-old calf was found alone and severely weakened in September. The rescue and rehabilitation teams, including the Wildlife Trust of India and the Assam Forest Department, arranged veterinary attention and frequent feeding. The calf weighed about 48 kilograms when brought to the centre on September 15. By October 23 her weight had reached 60 kilograms, and she was becoming more active and beginning to try vegetation alongside milk formula. Her rehabilitation remains ongoing. She has not yet been returned to the wild, and any future release will depend on her health and ability to live independently.
